title: Simon on bass, father teaching the sons, first guitar
summary: Their father taught all the sons; Simon became the bass player; Lawrence's first instrument was a six-string guitar shown by John.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Yeah, I'm sure. That's what everybody says, yeah.
Yeah, one of the best routines. Both of them, my brother Simon and my father.
Maybe you can tell us a little bit about Simon. How did he play anything else besides bass? Oh yeah, he was a sousaphone player. Oh, did he play in brass bands or anything? Yeah.
He was, then he played with a drum player, bass drum player like myself.
Oh yeah. Yeah, he was pretty good. I suppose you know who he learned from? Mostly your father I guess and around the family.
Most of my father taught them, taught all of us how to handle our instruments.
When they were young, did they all play your father's bass? Did they get instruments right away or what?

No, they didn't get them. They all, we all learned on one of the instruments. Uh-huh. See? And I did pick up sousaphone one time, but it was a little difficult for me so I wouldn't bother with it anymore. But the bass, I also did pick up the bass. I used to play bass. Yeah, I was in the first class bass, but I could play.
But my brother, he continued on and he made a good bass player.
Do you remember the very first instrument you got? Was it the guitar or banjo? It was a guitar. It was a guitar.
It was a guitar. Six string, was it?
Six string guitar. Six string. Yeah. And your brother then showed you some of the cards and the- He showed me all the cards of the 100.

Yeah, Bill Nath. If he wouldn't have died so early, I'd have been better off than I am today. I'd have been a more better musician. Because what the music I know and what he would teach me, that would give me a lot of advancements, Bill.
